% Frozen isolated candidate.  This file is not a live-book input.
% No claim of priority is made.  Production Rethlas verification is pending.

Work with the standing parlinear parameters
\(K=\mathbf Q\) and \(G=\mathbf R\) used in the body of
Chambert--Loir--Ducros.  Let \(Z\) be a locally compact Hausdorff space
with a basis of clopen subsets.  Give
\(Z\) the following affine \(G\)-tropical structure: its domains are the
locally closed subsets, and its parlinear and affine functions are the
locally constant real-valued functions.  Let
\(\Omega\subseteq\mathbf R^d\), \(d\geq0\), be a nonempty open convex set
with its
standard affine structure, and give
\[
                         X=Z\times\Omega
\]
the product affine \(G\)-tropical structure of
\cite[\S\S9.1.1--9.1.4]{CLD25}.  Thus a function on \(X\) is smooth precisely when,
locally on \(Z\times\Omega\), it is independent of the \(Z\)-variable and
smooth in the Euclidean variable.  Such a smooth function is psh precisely
when its Euclidean Hessian is positive semidefinite.

Write \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}\),
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\), and \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\) for the smooth
psh generator sheaf, its first local decreasing-limit stage, and the full
generated CLD psh sheaf, respectively.  Then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-collapse}
                    \operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}
                    =\operatorname{Psh}_X.
\end{equation}
More precisely, for every \(u\in\operatorname{Psh}_X(U)\) and every
\((z_0,x_0)\in U\), there are a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\) of
\(z_0\) and an open Euclidean ball \(B_0\) about \(x_0\), with
\(C\times\overline{B_0}\subseteq U\), such that the following fixed-
neighbourhood re-selection holds.  For every ball \(B\) about \(x_0\) with
\(\overline B\subseteq B_0\), there are smooth psh functions
\(g_k\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}(C\times B)\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-fixed-neighbourhood}
                          g_{k+1}\leq g_k,
             \qquad      g_k\downarrow u|_{C\times B}.
\end{equation}

The local comparison class used in the proof has an intrinsic
factorization description.  After shrinking \(C\times B\), every section
of \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\) can be written
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-factorization}
             u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x),
\end{equation}
where \(q:C\twoheadrightarrow Y\) is a continuous surjection onto a compact
metrizable zero-dimensional space, \(\bar u\) is upper semicontinuous on
\(Y\times B\), and, for every \(y\in Y\), the function
\(x\mapsto\bar u(y,x)\) is either finite-valued convex or identically
\(-\infty\).  Conversely, every function locally admitting
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factorization} with these properties belongs to
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\).

In particular, the conclusion applies for arbitrary \(d\) and to the
nonmetrizable, nonambient examples
\[
                    Z=\{0,1\}^{\Lambda}
\]
for every index set \(\Lambda\), including uncountable \(\Lambda\), with
the locally constant affine structure just specified.  The result concerns
this exact product structure; it makes no assertion for a different affine
structure on the same underlying space, for general polyhedral face
gluings, or for arbitrary affine \(G\)-tropical spaces.

# P07.1 Stone-parameter × Euclidean candidate: source and obligation matrix

## Status and exact scope

This is an isolated candidate packet. It has not been inserted into the
live manuscript and has not yet passed a production Rethlas call. It proves
a first-stage collapse statement only for the exact product affine
G-tropical structure specified in statement.tex.

The candidate does **not** retire P07.1. The remaining bridge is from this
product geometry to arbitrary affine G-tropical local models, especially
models with nontrivial affine directions in the parameter factor or
polyhedral face gluing.

## Primary source ledger

| Source | Exact use | Local fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| A. Chambert-Loir and A. Ducros, *Formes différentielles réelles et courants sur les espaces de Berkovich*, arXiv:1204.6277v2 (25 July 2025), cited as CLD25 | Standing parlinear parameters; G-tropical and affine axioms; smooth forms; products; positivity; psh generation and first stage; Euclidean convexity | Navigation extraction /private/tmp/CLD25.txt, SHA-256 021be260392de1f3240858d4c775da86653518dfab4fd9c4c21a2406081b6c7e |

The extraction is used only to audit section numbering. The cited
mathematical source is the official arXiv v2 article. All other ingredients
below are elementary topology or Euclidean convex analysis and are proved
at the point of use.

## Source-legality matrix

| ID | Obligation | Discharge in the packet | Source / exact boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | Fix legal parlinear parameters | statement.tex explicitly fixes \(K=\mathbf Q\), \(G=\mathbf R\) | CLD §1.8.2. No claim is made for a smaller \(G\). |
| S1 | Verify the CLD topological axiom | First proof block: a locally compact Hausdorff space with a clopen basis has a basis of relatively compact opens, hence of opens countable at infinity | CLD §3.1.1 plus the internal one-line shrinking argument |
| S2 | Verify all four domain axioms | Domains are all locally closed subsets; compact clopen neighbourhoods in each locally closed subspace give the compact-domain G-cover | CLD §3.1.2; proved explicitly |
| S3 | Verify the parlinear G-sheaf and its three axioms | The proof checks G-gluing, finite polyhedral image on compact domains, stability under composition, and the domain property for inverse images | CLD §3.1.3 and §§1.8.1–1.8.3; proved explicitly |
| S4 | Verify the affine refinement | Set \(L_Z=\operatorname{PL}_Z\); ordinary gluing and “parlinear iff G-locally affine” are checked | CLD §6.1.1 |
| S5 | Form the product source legally | Use the CLD product construction, not the full locally closed product site | CLD §§9.1.1–9.1.4 |
| S6 | Identify smooth generators and positivity | Product affine coordinates are locally constant in \(Z\) plus affine in \(x\); after clopen shrinking smooth functions depend only on \(x\), and positivity is positive semidefiniteness of the Euclidean Hessian | CLD Definition 6.2.1, Definition 3.5.1, Example 3.5.4, and Proposition 8.3.2 |
| S7 | Identify the generated and first-stage sheaves | The minimality step uses the smallest decreasing-limit-stable subsheaf; the final step produces local decreasing smooth-psh sequences | CLD Definition 8.1.1, Lemma 8.1.4, Definition 8.1.13 |

## Proof-obligation matrix

| ID | Obligation | Exact mechanism | Packet locator | Status |

| Q2 | Contain every smooth psh generator | Clopen shrinking kills the \(Z\)-dependence and the quotient may be a point | Paragraph after \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-local-factor}\) | Discharged |
| F1 | Fuse countably many rowwise/local quotients | A finite product cover for each row supplies countably many clopen generators; their Boolean algebra defines one evaluation quotient \(q:C\to Y\) | \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factor-cover}\)–\(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-common-quotient}\) | Discharged |
| F2 | Prove factorization through the common quotient | Equality of evaluation coordinates forces equality in every local quotient, because a countable clopen base separates points | Paragraph before \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-limit-factor}\) | Discharged |
| U1 | Descend upper semicontinuity to \(Y\times B_0\) | The proof avoids assuming that a product quotient is automatically quotient: it uses compact fibres, a finite product-neighbourhood subcover, and closedness of \(q\) | \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-sublevel-union}\)–\(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-quotient-neighbourhood}\) | Discharged |

| R2 | Verify smooth gluing across parameter pieces | The pullbacks \(q^{-1}(P)\) form a finite clopen partition, so branchwise Euclidean smooth convex functions are globally smooth psh on \(C\times B\) | Paragraph after \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-smoothed-envelope}\) | Discharged |
| R3 | Restore exact cross-level monotonicity | The displayed three-step inequality gives \(w_{k+1}\le w_k+\eta_{k+1}\); summable tail constants absorb the error | \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-almost-monotone}\)–\(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-tail-correction}\) | Discharged |
| R4 | Identify the final limit | \(0\le w_k-a_k\le\eta_k\), \(a_k\downarrow\bar v\), and the tail constants tend to zero | Paragraph after \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-tail-correction}\) | Discharged |
| Z0 | Treat \(d=0\) rather than silently invoking convolution | Use only the nested clopen partitions and floors; the approximants are locally constant smooth psh | \(\eqref{eq:p071-stone-zero-dimensional-envelope}\) | Discharged |
| B1 | Preserve scope and novelty firewalls | The statement explicitly excludes other affine structures, face gluings, and arbitrary affine G-tropical spaces; no priority claim is made | Last paragraph of statement.tex | Discharged |

## Dependency-free points

The Boolean-quotient construction does not invoke a representation theorem
for Stone spaces. It is the explicit evaluation map into the countable cube
indexed by the generated Boolean algebra. Likewise, the USC descent does
not invoke a general theorem about products of quotient maps. These two
potentially delicate bridges are proved directly in proof.tex.

# Hostile boundary audit

## Verdict before production verification

**No fatal mathematical gap was found in the exact product-scope
candidate.** This is an internal audit only, not a Rethlas verdict and not
authorization to integrate the result into the live book.

## Failure attempts

### 1. Nonmetrizable parameter space

An uncountable Cantor cube is not first countable or metrizable, so one
cannot regularize directly in its topology. The proof uses only countably
many local quotient data, because a CLD successor operation is sequential
and each row has a finite cover of the compact core. The generated Boolean
algebra is countable, hence its evaluation quotient is compact metrizable.
No metrizability of \(Z\) is imported.

### 2. Shrinking row neighbourhoods

The proof does not select from the original row approximants. It first
places the full generated sheaf inside a comparison sheaf stable under
decreasing limits, then constructs a fresh approximation from the single
factorization of the limit germ on \(C\times B_0\). Thus the original
shrinking-neighbourhood obstruction is genuinely bypassed in this product
scope.

### 3. Product-quotient USC gap

The assertion that \(\bar v\) is USC is not inferred merely from continuity
of \(q\). For a strict sublevel, compactness of \(q^{-1}(y)\) gives one
finite product neighbourhood contained in the pulled-back sublevel, and
closedness of \(q\) produces an open neighbourhood downstairs. This closes
the common product-quotient gap.

### 4. Fibrewise \(-\infty\)

The comparison class does not permit a partly polar convex fibre. The
midpoint argument proves that a locally convex
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued function on a connected ball is either
finite everywhere or identically \(-\infty\). The floors \(-k\) make every
upper envelope finite, and joint USC proves convergence even at a polar
point.

### 5. Supremum could be infinite

The shifts used in one envelope remain in the compact set
\(\overline{B_1}+r_1\overline{\mathbb B}\Subset B_0\). A
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued USC function is bounded above on the
resulting compact product with \(Y\). Hence every envelope is finite after
the floor.

### 6. Smoothing could break monotonicity

Different levels use different convolution radii, so monotonicity does not
survive literally. Jensen and the finite-family approximation estimate
give the exact chain
\[
 w_{k+1}\le a_{k+1}+\eta_{k+1}
 \le a_k+\eta_{k+1}\le w_k+\eta_{k+1}.
\]
The summable tail constants then make the corrected sequence exactly
decreasing.

### 7. Positivity at clopen seams

There are no seams in the local topology: every
\(q^{-1}(P)\) is clopen in \(Z\). Near each point a smoothed approximant is
one Euclidean smooth convex branch, so it is smooth psh for the exact
product affine structure.

### 8. Degenerate Euclidean factor

The proof treats \(d=0\) separately. The approximants are finite-level
locally constant functions, so no nonexistent convolution or strict ball
nesting is used.

### 9. Illegal choice of parlinear parameters

For a smaller value group \(G\), an arbitrary finite subset of
\(\mathbf R^m\) need not be a legal \(G\)-polyhedron. The statement
therefore fixes CLD's body convention \(K=\mathbf Q,G=\mathbf R\).
Dropping this hypothesis has not been audited.

### 10. A hidden claim for another affine structure

The proof uses decisively that all parameter-direction affine functions are
locally constant. A different affine structure on the same topological
space can add Hessian directions or coupling conditions and is outside the
statement.

## Exact surviving boundary

The following cases remain outside the packet:

- nontrivial affine directions in the parameter factor;
- polyhedral face gluing and junction positivity constraints;
- arbitrary affine G-tropical spaces;
- a counterexample genuinely requiring the second CLD stage;
- any uniform early ordinal for the remaining geometries.

Accordingly, the packet narrows P07.1 but does not solve or retire it, and
it gives no result on P07.2.

# Independent exact-byte hostile/source audit

## Frozen-byte binding

This audit binds exactly the following candidate bytes:

- `statement.tex`: `dfd8c7cc9d6d26f50260707975ff62d4f292627f084400bcd37b32253c876cdc`
- `proof.tex`: `9316e1a9df86c73a68ec099d3254e451ceaaac17a15c2a92441ad44961d863f6`

The hashes were computed before the audit and rechecked after it.  The
candidate statement and proof were not edited, and the candidate was not
submitted to production Rethlas as part of this audit.

## Numbered verdict

1. **SHA/freeze: PASS.**  Both exact SHA-256 values match the frozen-byte
   binding above.

2. **CLD source legality: PASS.**  Local compactness together with the
   clopen-basis hypothesis gives a compact-clopen local base, hence the
   topological hypothesis of CLD Section 3.1.1.  Taking every locally closed
   subset as a domain satisfies all four axioms in Section 3.1.2.  Locally
   constant functions satisfy G-gluing and all the parlinear axioms in
   Section 3.1.3; on a compact domain their image is finite, hence is a legal
   compact polyhedron for the standing `(Q,R)` parameters.  Taking the
   affine presheaf equal to the parlinear sheaf satisfies Section 6.1.1, and
   the product is the legal CLD product of Sections 9.1.1--9.1.4.

3. **Product smooth/psh characterization: PASS.**  Product affine
   coordinates split locally into a locally constant term in `Z` and an
   affine term in the Euclidean variable.  After an ordinary, equivalently
   clopen, shrinking in `Z`, the former is constant.  Definition 6.2.1 then
   gives precisely the functions locally independent of `Z` and smooth in
   the Euclidean variable; the identity chart on the Euclidean factor gives
   the converse.  The positivity condition is exactly positive
   semidefiniteness of the Euclidean Hessian, with the `d=0` case vacuous.

4. **Comparison sheaf and minimality: PASS.**  The factorization condition
   is local and therefore defines a genuine subsheaf.  It contains every
   smooth psh generator after a clopen shrinking.  Once sequential closure
   is proved, the minimality in CLD Definition 8.1.1 yields the claimed
   inclusion from the full psh sheaf.

5. **Countable Stone quotient construction: PASS.**  For each row,
   compactness of the common core gives a finite product cover by local
   factorizations.  Across the countably many rows, the resulting clopen
   generators generate a countable Boolean algebra.  Its evaluation map has
   compact, metrizable, zero-dimensional image.  Membership in the recorded
   clopens and separation by each local quotient's countable clopen base
   prove that every row is constant on the fibres of the common
   `q x id` map.

6. **Upper-semicontinuity descent: PASS.**  A decreasing limit of the local
   upper-semicontinuous rows has open strict sublevel sets.  For a point of a
   descended strict sublevel, compactness of the fibre gives a finite family
   of product neighbourhoods.  Their union/intersection construction and
   closedness of the compact-to-Hausdorff map `q` produce a product
   neighbourhood downstairs.  Thus joint upper semicontinuity is proved
   without assuming, unsupportedly, that `q x id` is automatically a
   quotient map.

7. **Extended convex dichotomy and passage to the limit: PASS.**  The local
   midpoint argument makes both the finite locus and the `-infinity` locus
   open.  Connectedness of the ball gives the dichotomy, and segment
   subdivision globalizes local convexity.  Convex inequalities pass through
   a decreasing finite-convex sequence; if the limit has one polar value, a
   slightly extended segment propagates it to every point.

8. **Sup-envelope monotonicity and convergence: PASS.**  Refinement of the
   nested clopen partitions, decrease of the radii, and decrease of the
   floors from `-k` to `-(k+1)` give exact cross-level monotonicity.  Mesh
   convergence together with joint upper semicontinuity identifies the
   pointwise limit at both finite and polar points.  In the finite-value case
   one also takes `k` large enough that the floor lies below the selected
   upper level; this is immediate and is merely an implicit phrase, not a
   proof gap.

9. **Euclidean mollification and tail correction: PASS.**  Each envelope
   branch is finite continuous convex.  Compact containment and finiteness of
   each partition give one mollification scale for that level.  Jensen's
   inequality supplies the lower error bound and uniform convergence supplies
   the upper one.  With
   `c_k = sum_{j >= k+1} eta_j`, the index identity
   `c_k = eta_{k+1} + c_{k+1}` converts almost monotonicity into
   `g_{k+1} <= g_k`; mollification errors and tails both vanish, so the limit
   is the required function.

10. **The case `d=0`: PASS.**  The partition envelopes are finite locally
    constant functions, hence smooth psh for the stated affine structure.
    Refinement and the floors make them decreasing, and upper
    semicontinuity plus shrinking mesh gives the asserted limit without
    convolution.

11. **Nonmetrizable cubes: PASS.**  For every index set `Lambda`, the cube
    `{0,1}^Lambda` is compact Hausdorff and zero-dimensional.  The proof never
    assumes that `Z` itself is metrizable: it explicitly constructs the
    countable metrizable quotient needed by each generated psh function.

12. **Scope firewall: PASS.**  The result concerns only the exact product
    with locally constant affine structure in the parameter direction.  It
    makes no inference for nontrivial affine parameter directions,
    polyhedral face gluings, or arbitrary affine G-tropical spaces.  It
    therefore narrows P07.1 but does not retire that open problem.

## Final audit status

**PASS: zero critical errors and zero unresolved proof/source gaps.**

This was an independent fail-closed audit of the exact bytes identified
above.  No priority claim was assessed.  The frozen candidate statement and
proof were not edited, and no production submission was made.

% Frozen isolated candidate proof.  This file is not a live-book input.
% Production Rethlas verification is pending.

We divide the proof into source-legality, a countable-factor comparison
sheaf, and a fixed-neighbourhood regularization.

First consider \(Z\) alone.  Its topology satisfies
\cite[\S3.1.1]{CLD25}: local compactness and the clopen-basis hypothesis
give a basis of relatively compact open subsets, hence a basis of open
subsets that are countable at infinity.  Locally closed subsets satisfy the
domain axioms of \cite[\S3.1.2]{CLD25}.  Indeed, the first three axioms are
immediate from the definition, and every locally closed subset is itself a
locally compact space with a clopen basis; its compact clopen
neighbourhoods form the required \(G\)-cover by compact domains.

The locally constant real-valued functions form a \(G\)-sheaf.  To check
the only nonformal point, suppose compatible locally constant functions are
glued across a \(G\)-cover.  At a given point, use the finite subfamily in
the definition of a \(G\)-cover.  Intersect ordinary neighbourhoods on
which the finitely many restrictions are constant.  Their union contains
a neighbourhood of the point in the domain, and compatibility makes the
glued function constant there.

A locally constant map from a compact domain has finite image.  In the
standing \((\mathbf Q,\mathbf R)\)-convention of
\cite[\S1.8.2]{CLD25}, every finite subset of \(\mathbf R^m\) is a compact
polyhedron.  Parlinear composition preserves local constancy.  The inverse
image of any subset under a locally constant map is clopen in its domain,
so in particular the inverse image of a parlinear subspace is a domain.
This verifies all the axioms in \cite[\S3.1.3]{CLD25}.

Take the affine presheaf \(L_Z\) equal to this parlinear sheaf.  It contains
the constants, ordinary local gluing preserves local constancy, and a
function is parlinear if and only if it is \(G\)-locally affine.  Thus the
two affinage axioms of \cite[\S6.1.1]{CLD25} hold.  Consequently the data
in the statement make \(Z\) an affine \(G\)-tropical space of tropical
dimension zero.

The product with the standard affine space \(\Omega\) is legitimate by
\cite[\S\S9.1.1--9.1.4]{CLD25}.  Product affine functions are locally sums
of locally constant functions of \(z\) and affine functions of \(x\).
It follows from \cite[Definition~6.2.1]{CLD25} that, after a clopen
shrinking in the \(Z\)-factor, a smooth function is a smooth function of
the Euclidean variable alone, and conversely.  The formula for
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''\) and positivity are therefore the ordinary
Hessian formula and positive-semidefiniteness on the Euclidean factor.
This proves source-legality and the asserted description of the smooth psh
generators.

Define \(\mathscr Q\) to be the sheaf of functions with values in
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) which locally have the following form.  There
are a compact clopen \(C\subseteq Z\), an open ball
\(B\Subset\Omega\), a compact metrizable space \(Y\) with a clopen basis, a
continuous surjection \(q:C\to Y\), and an upper semicontinuous function
\(\bar v:Y\times B\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-local-factor}
                  v(z,x)=\bar v(q(z),x),
\end{equation}
and, for every \(y\in Y\), \(x\mapsto\bar v(y,x)\) is either finite-valued
convex or identically \(-\infty\).  This is a sheaf because the condition
is local.  Every smooth psh function belongs to
\(\mathscr Q\): shrink until it is independent of \(z\), take \(Y\) to be
a point, and use positivity of its Euclidean Hessian.

We next prove that \(\mathscr Q\) is stable under decreasing sequential
limits.  Let \(v_n\downarrow v\) on an open subset \(W\) of \(X\), with
every \(v_n\in\mathscr Q(W)\), and fix a point.  Choose a compact clopen
\(C\subseteq Z\) and a ball \(B_0\Subset\Omega\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-compact-core}
                         C\times\overline{B_0}\subseteq W.
\end{equation}
For each
fixed \(n\), compactness gives a finite cover of
\(C\times\overline{B_0}\) by product sets
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-factor-cover}
                       C_{n,a}\times B_{n,a},
\end{equation}
where \(C_{n,a}\) is compact clopen in \(C\), \(B_{n,a}\) is open, and on this
product \(v_n\) factors through a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
quotient \(q_{n,a}:C_{n,a}\to Y_{n,a}\).

Choose a countable clopen base \(\mathcal D_{n,a}\) of every \(Y_{n,a}\).
Let \(\mathcal B\) be the Boolean subalgebra of the clopen subsets of \(C\)
generated by all the sets \(C_{n,a}\) and all the sets
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-boolean-generators}
                  q_{n,a}^{-1}(D),
                  \qquad D\in\mathcal D_{n,a}.
\end{equation}
viewed as clopen subsets of \(C\).  There are countably many generators.
Declare two points of \(C\) equivalent when they belong to the same members
of \(\mathcal B\), and let
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-common-quotient}
                  q:C\longrightarrow
                  Y:=q(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}.
\end{equation}
Every coordinate of \(q\) is the characteristic function of a clopen set,
so \(q\) is continuous and is surjective by the definition of \(Y\).
The space \(Y\) is compact, metrizable, and zero-dimensional.

Every \(v_n|_{C\times B_0}\) is constant on the fibres of
\(q\times\operatorname{id}_{B_0}\).  Indeed, if \(q(z)=q(z')\) and
\(x\in B_0\), choose a member of the finite cover
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factor-cover} containing
\((z,x)\).  Membership in \(C_{n,a}\) is recorded in \(\mathcal B\), so
\(z'\in C_{n,a}\).  Membership in the inverse images of the countable
clopen base separates the points of \(Y_{n,a}\), hence
\(q_{n,a}(z)=q_{n,a}(z')\), and the local factorization gives
\(v_n(z,x)=v_n(z',x)\).  It follows that the decreasing limit \(v\) factors
as
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-limit-factor}
                         v(z,x)=\bar v(q(z),x).
\end{equation}

The function \(\bar v\) is upper semicontinuous.  Here is the quotient
argument, included to avoid an unsupported product-quotient assertion.
For \(t\in\mathbf R\), the set \(\{v<t\}\) is open because
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-sublevel-union}
                       \{v<t\}=\bigcup_n\{v_n<t\}.
\end{equation}
If \(\bar v(y,x)<t\), then, for every \(z\in q^{-1}(y)\), choose open
sets \(N_z\ni z\) and \(D_z\ni x\) whose product lies in \(\{v<t\}\).
A finite subcover of the compact fibre gives
\(N=\bigcup_zN_z\) and \(D=\bigcap_zD_z\), where the union and intersection
are now over that finite subcover; then
\(N\times D\subseteq\{v<t\}\).  The map \(q\) is closed because its source
is compact and its target is Hausdorff.  Therefore
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-quotient-neighbourhood}
                       Y\setminus q(C\setminus N)
\end{equation}
is an open neighbourhood of \(y\), and its product with \(D\) is contained
in \(\{\bar v<t\}\).  Thus all strict sublevel sets of \(\bar v\) are open.

We include the extended-value point in the fibrewise convexity argument.
A locally extended-real convex function
\(h:B_0\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is either finite everywhere or
identically \(-\infty\).  On a sufficiently small ball of local convexity,
if \(h(a)=-\infty\), every point of a smaller ball about \(a\) lies
strictly between \(a\) and another point of the first ball, so convexity
forces the smaller ball to have value \(-\infty\).  If \(h(a)\) is finite,
the same midpoint argument excludes \(-\infty\) on a smaller ball.  Hence
the \(-\infty\)-locus and its complement are open; connectedness of \(B_0\)
proves the dichotomy.  In the finite case, subdivision of line segments
shows that local convexity implies convexity on \(B_0\).

Apply this observation to \(x\mapsto v_n(z,x)\), for a fixed \(z\).  If one
term is identically \(-\infty\), all later terms and the limit are as well.
Otherwise all terms are finite and convex.  Passing to the limit in their
convexity inequalities shows that the limit is extended-real convex.  If
it is \(-\infty\) at one point, then, for any other point, use a slightly
longer segment inside the open convex ball and the convexity inequality to
force the value at that point to be \(-\infty\).  This is the elementary
argument used in \cite[Proposition~8.3.2]{CLD25}.  Otherwise the limit is
finite and convex.  By \eqref{eq:p071-stone-limit-factor}, this is exactly
the required statement for every fibre of \(\bar v\).  We have proved that
\(\mathscr Q\) is stable under decreasing limits.

The sheaf \(\mathscr Q\) contains every smooth psh generator and is stable
under the defining operation of \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\).  Minimality in
\cite[Definition~8.1.1]{CLD25} therefore gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-minimality}
                         \operatorname{Psh}_X\subseteq\mathscr Q.
\end{equation}

It remains to prove the reverse inclusion into the first stage, and this is
where the representatives are re-selected on one fixed neighbourhood.  Let
\(v\in\mathscr Q\) have a representation
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-local-factor} on \(C\times B_0\).  Suppose first that
\(d>0\), fix any ball \(B\) with \(\overline B\subseteq B_0\), and choose a
ball \(B_1\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-nested-balls}
                 \overline B\subseteq B_1,
                 \qquad \overline{B_1}\subseteq B_0
\end{equation}
and positive radii \(r_k\downarrow0\) such that
\(\overline{B_1}+r_1\overline{\mathbb B}\subseteq B_0\).  Give \(Y\) a
compatible metric.  Compactness and the clopen-basis property give nested
finite clopen partitions \(\mathcal P_k\) whose mesh tends to zero: at
stage \(k\), take a finite clopen cover of mesh less than \(2^{-k}\) and
refine it together with all preceding covers.  For
\(P\in\mathcal P_k\) and \(x\in B_1\), put
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-upper-envelope}
 a_{k,P}(x)=
 \max\left\{-k,
   \sup_{\substack{y\in P\\ |\xi|\leq r_k}}
          \bar v(y,x+\xi)\right\}.
\end{equation}
Upper semicontinuity bounds \(\bar v\) from above on the compact set
\(Y\times(\overline{B_1}+r_1\overline{\mathbb B})\).  Thus the supremum in
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-upper-envelope} is finite from above, and the
truncation makes \(a_{k,P}\) real-valued.  It is convex, being the maximum
of a constant and a supremum of translates of convex functions, and hence
is continuous on \(B_1\).  If \(P_k(y)\) denotes the member of
\(\mathcal P_k\) containing
\(y\), define
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-piecewise-envelope}
                         a_k(y,x)=a_{k,P_k(y)}(x).
\end{equation}
The refinement of the partitions, the decrease of \(r_k\), and the lower
truncations \(-k\) give
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-envelope-monotonicity}
                          a_{k+1}\leq a_k.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-envelope-convergence}
                          a_k\downarrow\bar v
\end{equation}
pointwise on \(Y\times B_1\).  To check the only nonformal assertion, fix
\((y,x)\).  The lower bound follows by taking \(\xi=0\) and the same \(y\)
in \eqref{eq:p071-stone-upper-envelope}.  If \(\bar v(y,x)\) is finite,
upper semicontinuity makes
\(\bar v\) smaller than \(\bar v(y,x)+\varepsilon\) on a product
neighbourhood; eventually \(P_k(y)\) lies in its \(Y\)-factor and
\(r_k\) lies in its Euclidean factor.  If \(\bar v(y,x)=-\infty\), apply
the same argument with an arbitrary finite upper level, also taking \(k\)
large enough that \(-k\) lies below that level, and then let the level tend
to \(-\infty\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-envelope-convergence}, including the polar case.

Choose positive numbers \(\eta_k\) with
\(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\).  Let \(\rho\) be a nonnegative smooth
probability kernel on \(\mathbf R^d\), supported in the unit ball and of
barycentre zero.  Since every \(a_{k,P}\) is a finite continuous convex
function and \(\mathcal P_k\) is finite, one can choose
\(\varepsilon_k>0\), with the convolution defined on \(B\), such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-mollification-error}
  0\leq
  (a_{k,P}*\rho_{\varepsilon_k})(x)-a_{k,P}(x)
  \leq\eta_k
  \quad(P\in\mathcal P_k,\ x\in B).
\end{equation}
The lower inequality is Jensen's inequality; the upper inequality is the
uniform convergence of mollifications on the compact set
\(\overline B\), applied to the finite family indexed by
\(\mathcal P_k\).

On \(q^{-1}(P)\times B\), define
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-smoothed-envelope}
                 w_k(z,x)=
                 (a_{k,P}*\rho_{\varepsilon_k})(x).
\end{equation}
The sets \(q^{-1}(P)\) form a finite clopen partition of \(C\), and each is
clopen in \(Z\).  Hence
\(w_k\) is smooth for the stated product affine structure.  Each branch in
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-smoothed-envelope} is smooth convex, so
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''w_k\geq0\).  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-envelope-monotonicity} and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-mollification-error} give
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-almost-monotone}
 w_{k+1}(z,x)
 \leq a_{k+1}(q(z),x)+\eta_{k+1}
 \leq a_k(q(z),x)+\eta_{k+1}
 \leq w_k(z,x)+\eta_{k+1}.
\end{equation}
Set
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-tail-correction}
                       c_k=\sum_{j\geq k+1}\eta_j,
             \qquad   g_k=w_k+c_k.
\end{equation}
Then \(c_k=\eta_{k+1}+c_{k+1}\), so
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-almost-monotone} implies \(g_{k+1}\leq g_k\).
Finally, \eqref{eq:p071-stone-envelope-convergence},
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-mollification-error}, and \(c_k\to0\) show
that \(g_k\downarrow v\) on \(C\times B\).  This proves the reverse
inclusion when \(d>0\).

If \(d=0\), the unique nonempty open subset of \(\mathbf R^0\) is a point.
Give \(Y\) a compatible metric and choose nested finite clopen partitions
\(\mathcal P_k\) whose mesh tends to zero, exactly as above.  Put
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-zero-dimensional-envelope}
        a_{k,P}=\max\{-k,\sup_{y\in P}\bar v(y)\},
        \qquad w_k(z)=a_{k,P_k(q(z))}.
\end{equation}
The functions \(w_k\) are locally constant, hence smooth psh.  Refinement
and the lower truncations show that they decrease.  Upper semicontinuity
and the shrinking mesh give \(w_k\downarrow v\), by the same argument as
for \eqref{eq:p071-stone-envelope-convergence}.  Thus the conclusion holds
without Euclidean mollification or a tail correction.

We have proved
\(\mathscr Q\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\) in every dimension.
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-stone-minimality} and the tautological
inclusion
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_X\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-collapse}--\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factorization}, as
well as the fixed-neighbourhood assertion
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-fixed-neighbourhood}.

For the displayed example, the Cantor cube \(\{0,1\}^{\Lambda}\) is compact,
Hausdorff, and zero-dimensional for every \(\Lambda\).  When \(\Lambda\) is
uncountable it is generally nonmetrizable, but every function produced by
the hierarchy locally factors through the metrizable quotient constructed
in \eqref{eq:p071-stone-common-quotient}; no metrizability of \(Z\) was
used.  This also makes clear why
the argument does not extend to a nontrivial affine structure in the
\(Z\)-direction or to general polyhedral face gluings.
